# Project workforce and orchestration

**Canonical for:** how the development workforce is governed, and which control
plane owns which state.

> Product/runtime agents and development workforce agents are NOT the same architecture. They share concepts (capability, workspace, approval, delegation) but differ in ownership, trust, deployment and lifecycle. A change to one is not automatically a change to the other, and neither may import the other's authority model.

## Two worlds

### product-runtime

- **Summary:** Agents executing user workloads inside n8n.
- **Members:** Agent Machine, AI Node, runtime adapters (Hermes, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenClaw)
- **Governed by:** manifest/ai-lego-set.json + manifest/ai-foundation.json
- **Trust:** declared per provider/runtime; external runtimes are never automatically trusted

### development-workforce

- **Summary:** Agents building the n8n LEGO repository itself.
- **Members:** Arena manager/orchestrator, Arena workers, agent-1 .. agent-6
- **Governed by:** this file + manifest/domains.json ownership + docs/LEGO_PARALLEL_RULES.md
- **Trust:** bounded by branch, assigned task and domain ownership

## Manager authority

- cross-domain project orchestration
- GitHub branch/PR/task management
- architecture arbitration
- task routing
- integration order
- protected-branch decisions
- external runtime policy
- contract publication ownership
- permission namespace conflicts
- workforce governance

## Worker authority

- its assigned branch
- its assigned task
- its workspace
- its permitted capabilities
- test/build execution
- contract updates strictly inside its ownership

### A worker may not

- resolve a manager-owned decision
- edit another agent's domain
- push to another agent's branch
- modify or force-push main
- reset another agent's branch to make a tree look synchronized
- self-select unrestricted work when a task assignment exists

> A worker nested under a manager does NOT inherit manager authority. This is the same invariant as Agent Machine delegation: nesting grants nothing, and every grant is explicit. Applying one rule to product agents and the opposite rule to development agents would mean the project does not actually believe the rule.

## The worker loop

1. enter the assigned branch
2. read repository state
3. read project protocol (.ai/constitution.md, .ai/master/)
4. read the current task
5. confirm owner and boundary
6. perform the work
7. run the relevant gates and tests
8. record evidence
9. commit
10. report status

> A worker must be able to complete this loop from the repository alone. Requiring a human to re-explain project context to every new worker is a documentation defect, not a workflow.

## Job and task model

Shape: **Job contains Tasks.**

Task fields: `taskId`, `jobId`, `owner`, `status`, `scope`, `dependencies`, `blockers`, `evidence`, `branch`, `expectedOutputs`, `validationGate`

- Moving a task to another job is an explicit state change, never a silent reinterpretation.
- A broad task may nominate a lead/orchestrator only where the manager protocol allows it.
- Simultaneous destructive edits are prevented by partitioning ownership, not by convention.

**Status:** contract-only — this repository declares the model; no task runtime is implemented here.

## Control planes

> Exactly one source of truth per kind of state. A second authoritative store for the same state is the defect, not the redundancy.

### github — code plane

- **Authoritative for:** repository state, branches, commits, pull requests, code review, source artifacts, implementation history
- **Rule:** GitHub is the source of truth for code. No second authoritative code registry may exist in Supabase, Obsidian, chat, agent memory or local notes.
- **Status:** active

### supabase — control plane

- **Authoritative for:** job/task state, agent coordination, worker state, task claims, orchestration metadata, evidence references
- **May not hold:** code, git history, a second copy of the repository
- **Rule:** Control-plane state only. Evidence is referenced, never duplicated.
- **Status:** NOT VERIFIED from this repository — no Supabase schema, client or credential exists in this tree. Any claim that a Supabase control path is operational must come from the manager, not from this file.

### vpsGate — execution gate

- **Authoritative for:** trusted build/test execution
- **Must declare:** gate health, allowed operations, workspace boundaries, authentication boundary, audit, secret sanitization, manager/worker policy, remote execution lifecycle
- **Rule:** The gate is a controlled capability boundary, NOT unrestricted shell access. It may expose capabilities without exposing raw secrets; credentials stay outside agent-visible payloads.
- **Status:** NOT VERIFIED from this repository — no gate client or endpoint is declared in this tree.

### obsidian — human knowledge projection

- **Authoritative for:** _nothing_
- **Rule:** A projection of the memory graph for humans. Never a hidden second source of truth; the memory graph must remain valid with no Obsidian connected.
- **Status:** contract-only

## Permanent decision principles

1. Contract before implementation.
2. One owner per responsibility.
3. No duplicate vocabulary.
4. Surface aliases do not create ownership.
5. Native local dispatch before network transport.
6. MCP is interoperability, not business architecture.
7. External runtimes remain external.
8. Skill is not an agent.
9. Capability is not implementation.
10. Memory is not context.
11. Context is not conversation.
12. Artifact is not event payload.
13. Approval is not permission inheritance.
14. Work Trace is not chain-of-thought.
15. Token telemetry is not merely UI decoration.
16. Nesting does not grant authority.
17. Zero-install is valid.
18. Resource-aware operation is first-class.
19. Rust is a measured optimization, not ideology.
20. Legacy must shrink.
21. Main is protected.
22. GitHub is source of truth for code.
23. Do not claim readiness that gates do not support.
24. A failed negative test is useful evidence.
25. Replaceable implementations must preserve contracts.
26. Agent completion is not merge approval.
27. Reconciliation PASS and MERGE PASS are separate gates.
28. A milestone is complete only after protected-main post-merge verification.
29. Contract and architecture conflicts must be reconciled before merge; never silently choose the easier branch.

## Runner protocol

**Authoritative document:** `docs/engineering-operations/RUNNER-PROTOCOL.md` (machine-readable: `docs/engineering-operations/workforce-governance.json#runnerProtocol`).

- **Architecture:** 5 Windows + 5 WSL self-hosted runners (10 total); do not reduce or change without a Manager decision.
- **Windows (5):** `laptop-build-worker`, `laptop-build-worker-2`, `laptop-build-worker-3`, `laptop-build-worker-4`, `laptop-build-worker-5` — labels `self-hosted, windows, x64, rust-build, n8n-rust`.
- **WSL (5):** `MDMTEST-n8n-wsl`, `MDMTEST-n8n-wsl-2`, `MDMTEST-n8n-wsl-3`, `MDMTEST-n8n-wsl-4`, `MDMTEST-n8n-wsl-5` — labels `self-hosted, linux, x64, rust-build, n8n-rust`.
- **Selection:** by label, never by runner name; at most 10 parallel self-hosted jobs.
- **Polling:** **1s** (max sleep 1s) — every wait for a runner, CI run, job, health endpoint, process or queue sleeps at most 1 second (prefer exactly 1s) inside a bounded attempt budget; no sleep 2/5/10/30/60, no setTimeout/setInterval above 1000 ms, no backoff step above 1s.
- **Only exception:** only a documented external API rate limit (name the API + limit next to the wait; honour Retry-After / x-ratelimit-reset).
- **Decoupling:** a loop wakes every <= 1s but may emit an expensive external call on its own slower cadence.
- **Job retry:** at most 2, only for environmental failures (runner lost, network, checkout/cache infrastructure).
- **Failure classes:** implementation, environmental, pre-existing, flaky.
- **Exhaustion:** jobs queue; the monitor keeps polling at 1s; after the job timeout the job is reported blocked (environmental) — never skipped, never moved to hosted runners to bypass the requirement.
- **GitHub Actions monitoring:** GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs at 1s until all completed; merge only with all checks success on the exact head SHA, pinned in the merge call.
- **VPS monitoring:** vps-runtime runner; 1s polling of /rest/settings (/healthz is 503 without the UI bundle); systemd supervises long-running processes.
- **Workspace lifecycle:** fresh checkout per job; temporary files under the runner temp directory; clean temp files, patches, logs, duplicate clones and stale worktrees; keep dependency/build caches; never commit runtime artifacts (.arena/gateway_tokens.json is gitignored); only main and arena-manager branches persist.

## Milestone merge and reconciliation protocol

**Canonical register:** `docs/n8n-lego/milestones.json`

> Agent branch completion is not merge approval. The reconciled and post-merge verified state on protected main is the milestone.

1. freeze baseline\n2. verify each branch and evidence\n3. reconcile contracts and dependencies\n4. classify conflicts\n5. run shared alignment and full relevant gates\n6. record reconciliation pass\n7. validate merge candidate against main\n8. merge only after merge pass\n9. rerun post-merge verification\n10. mark milestone complete only after protected-main verification

**Failure state:** `RECONCILIATION_FAILED`

- **mechanical:** Manager may resolve compatible file/path/generated-artifact conflicts.\n- **contract:** Reconcile fields, operations, enums, permissions and errors before merging.\n- **architecture:** Record and decide before merging; do not choose the easier implementation silently.\n- **scope:** Do not merge out-of-scope runtime, Memory, Workspace authority or Rust work merely to clean it up later.
